Sources in detail

The gotchas below are the ones that change a number if you miss them.

NEAR RPC

Archival JSON-RPC at archival-rpc.mainnet.fastnear.com: block by height for total supply, validators for stake, EXPERIMENTAL_protocol_config for the issuance ceiling, and call_function on meta-pool.near and linear-protocol.near for liquid staking prices.

  • The config field protocol_reward_rate reads as a fraction, but nearcore hard-codes the treasury's share on mainnet. The figures use the declared constant treasury_share from thesis/constants.toml, pinned to the nearcore source line, so stakers get the remainder.
  • Stake from validators trails the current epoch, so the staked share lags slightly.
  • The archival endpoint rate-limits. The sample cache is append-only, a missing sample stays missing, and a window edge with no sample nearby is null.
  • The history file's last row is the latest block, not the start of a day. It sets the “now” figures (supply, staked share, the rate in force); trailing windows end at the latest start-of-day sample instead.

BigQuery public dataset

bigquery-public-data.crypto_near_mainnet_us, queried with the SQL in sql/, always filtered on block_date.

  • The dataset lives in us-east1, and token amounts are FLOAT64 in yoctoNEAR, so sums lose precision at the last digits.
  • Before the developer gas rebate ended (HSP-027, at block 223,012,337 on 2026-11-04), tokens_burnt overstates the burn, because part of every function-call fee went to the called contract as a reward. From that block the whole fee burns, so gross equals net. The exact burn comes from per-block changes in total supply.
  • The dataset stopped updating for long stretches. The status board shows its last block date, and the burn chart says which method it used.

FRED

One keyless fredgraph.csv?id= request per series: fed funds (DFF, EFFR), the target range, CPI, core CPI, PCE, money supply, the euro exchange rate and the Fed's median projections. The desk simulation adds two: the euro short-term rate, €STR (ECBESTRVOLWGTTRMDMNRT, the European Central Bank's volume-weighted overnight rate, which FRED republishes), and the one-year Treasury yield (DGS1).

  • The desk reads each rate on or before the latest date every input shares, the same rule as the effective fed funds rate, so no rate comes from a day the price data has not reached.
  • FRED serves the latest vintage only, so a revised month changes history on the next pull.
  • The BLS skipped one month of CPI during the federal shutdown. Lines break there, year-over-year values that need that month are null, and windows that start or end in it move to the nearest month inside the window.

BIS

Central bank policy rates (WS_CBPOL) and consumer price inflation (WS_LONG_CPI) for the currency panel.

  • Australia publishes CPI quarterly; the monthly series repeats each quarter's value, and the chart flags it.
  • Argentina is excluded: its central bank stopped publishing a policy rate.

Binance and Coinbase prices

Daily candles from data-api.binance.vision for NEAR, bitcoin and ether, and Coinbase's NEAR-USD as a cross-check and fallback.

  • Binance quotes against USDT, not dollars. The cross-check against Coinbase's dollar price measures the gap.
  • Coinbase's NEAR history starts later than Binance's, so a Coinbase fallback omits the early windows and lists them.

Derivatives venues

Deribit, OKX and Aevo instrument lists for options, and Deribit's volatility indexes for bitcoin and ether.

  • An unreachable venue reads “not checked”, never “no”, and counts separately.

DefiLlama

Daily NEAR Intents volume and fees from DefiLlama's summary/dexs/near-intents and summary/fees/near-intents.

  • DefiLlama's figures come from a Dune table maintained by NEAR, so they are not independent of Dune. The Explorer cross-check exists to test that.
  • The most recent days are provisional and often revised upward; the Intents volume chart uses complete months only.

Money for the 10 most-traded currencies

One public, keyless money series per currency, from the publisher that issues it: FRED for the dollar, the ECB for the euro, the Bank of Japan for the yen, the Bank of England for sterling, the OECD for the yuan, the SNB for the franc, the RBA for the Australian dollar, the Bank of Canada for the Canadian dollar, the HKMA for the Hong Kong dollar, and SingStat, via the MAS, for the Singapore dollar. Each raw file under data/raw/money/<currency>/ has a sidecar with its URL, units and fetch time.

  • Units differ by publisher (millions, billions, index points); the loader reads each sidecar's unit string and refuses a unit it does not know.
  • Each currency's money growth is its latest twelve months, ending at its latest published month; nothing is filled or carried forward.
  • The Bank of England refuses repeated requests, so the pull makes one paced request per series and keeps the previous file when refused.
  • The OECD's monetary aggregates mirror several national series; cross-check X9 compares them.

BIS Triennial Survey ranking

The 10 currencies are ranked by daily turnover from the survey annex's table of turnover by currency, net-net, read from the BIS statistics API (dataflow WS_DER_OTC_TOV) by pipeline/sources/bis_fx.py into data/raw/bis_fx/; the annex PDF is the cross-check. The code sorts and takes the top ten; nobody types the list. The ranking uses the annex's later vintage of the figures (the survey's press page carries an earlier total), from the survey month 2025-04, and holds until the next survey.

NEAR Intents Explorer

The partner API at explorer.near-intents.org/api/v0. It needs a partner access token from NEAR Intents and allows one request every few seconds.

  • Raw rows are aggregated in memory and never written to disk, per NEAR Intents Terms of Service, section 4.1(e).
  • Published aggregates wait for written permission; see licences and terms.

Formulas

One anchor per formula id. Every number in the registry names one of these. Ids: F is a computed value, D a value read directly from a source, K a declared constant, P a parameter set in thesis/rules.toml, and X, further down, a cross-check between two sources.

F-growth Supply growth over a window

g = (S1 / S0) ^ (365.25 / days) - 1

S is total supply from the RPC sample nearest each window edge, and days come from the two blocks' timestamps. Samples are the block at the start of a UTC day: monthly from launch, then weekly, then daily (rpc/history_samples.csv merged with rpc/dense_samples.csv; on a date both files sampled they must agree exactly). Every trailing window ends at the latest of these full-day samples, so with daily samples a trailing year spans exactly one year. If no sample sits within a week of an edge, the value is null, never approximated.

Used by: g_365, g_365_at_m2, g_365_at_m2_from, g_since_cut, g_since_cut_from, g_since_cut_to, g_y_lst_365

F-ceiling Most the protocol allowed over the same window

ceiling = exp( sum_k  i_k * dt_k ) - 1      (i_k = max_inflation_rate in force, dt_k in years)

The issuance ceiling compounded over the time each value was in force, from EXPERIMENTAL_protocol_config. The rate switches at the exact first block of each change, found by bisecting the config between two sampled blocks (rpc/protocol_changes.csv), so the ceiling is exact rather than bracketed.

Used by: ceiling_365, ceiling_gap_dir

F-burnshare Burn as a share of issuance, exact

burn_share = sum(burn) / sum(mint)

Mint and burn from per-block changes in BigQuery's total supply. Used only when coverage of the window is complete.

Used by: burn_method, burn_method_short, burn_per_day_365, burn_share_365, mint_per_day_365, n_burn_epochs_365

F-burn-epochs Burn as a share of issuance, exact from every epoch boundary

minted     = sum_b minted_b      over every epoch boundary b with start_height < b <= end_height
burnt      = minted - (supply(end) - supply(start))
burn_share = burnt / minted
minted_b   = supply(b) - supply(b - 1) + burn in block b

Total supply moves only by the mint at the first block of each epoch and by the burn in every block, so over the exact window between two midnight UTC samples a year apart the burn is the summed mint less supply growth. No epoch is sampled or skipped: rpc/epoch_mints.csv walks back from the tip one boundary at a time, and each row records the boundary before it (prev_boundary_height). The method is used only when those links run unbroken from a boundary at or before the window start to one after its end; a gap or a missing link falls back to the monthly sample, and the burn chart says why. It must sit at or below the upper bound (cross-check). Labeled “exact: every epoch boundary” wherever it appears.

Used by: burn_share_365_epochs

F-burn-sampled Burn as a share of issuance, one epoch per month

burn_share = sum_e burnt_e / sum_e minted_e      (one complete epoch e per calendar month)
burnt_e  = supply(start) - supply(end) + burn in the start block
minted_e = supply(next start) - supply(end) + burn in the next start block

Each sampled epoch's mint and burn are exact RPC reads (rpc/epoch_history.csv). Only one epoch a month is read, so a single unusual epoch stands in for its whole month: the burn chart lists every sampled epoch, keeps the outliers, and shows the upper bound beside the sampled share. Used when neither BigQuery nor every epoch boundary covers the period (the calendar years), kept beside an exact trailing-year share for comparison, and labeled “sampled: one epoch per month” wherever it appears.

Used by: burn_share_365_sampled, n_burn_epochs_365_sampled

F-mint-check Realized mint against the ceiling, per epoch

gap_e = minted_e * seconds_per_year / (supply(start) * epoch_seconds) - max_inflation_rate      (pp)

Since nearcore's RectifyInflation protocol version (declared constant rectify_inflation_protocol), an epoch's reward is the ceiling rate times supply times the epoch's duration, so a full-online epoch mints at the ceiling and validators below the online threshold leave part unminted. Earlier epochs were paid by block count and are listed but not compared. One complete epoch per month (rpc/epoch_history.csv).

Used by: mint_check_365_method, mint_check_from, mint_vs_ceiling_max_365_pp, mint_vs_ceiling_median_365_pp, mint_vs_ceiling_min_365_pp, n_mint_epochs_365

F-burn-ub Burn plus unminted, upper bound

burn + unminted <= S0 * (exp(i * years) - 1) - (S1 - S0)

The gap between what the ceiling would mint and what supply actually did bounds the burn from above: the true share cannot exceed it. It is the measured share only when neither BigQuery, every epoch boundary nor a month-by-month epoch sample covers the period, and it is drawn beside the measured share in every period. Labeled “upper bound” wherever it appears.

Used by: burn_share_365_ub

F-lst Liquid staking yield

y = (P_end / P_start) ^ (365.25 / days) - 1      (P = stNEAR or LiNEAR price in NEAR)
y_lst = mean(y_stNEAR, y_LiNEAR) where both exist

A realized yield, net of validator commission and protocol fees, read from each token's on-chain exchange rate.

Used by: y_li_365, y_lst_365, y_lst_90, y_st_365

F-share Change in a holder's share of all NEAR

staker     = (1 + y_lst) / (1 + g) - 1
non_staker = 1 / (1 + g) - 1

Annualized per window. Positive means the holder owns a larger fraction of all NEAR at the end than at the start.

Used by: nonstaker_365, staker_share_365

F-yoy Year-over-year change

yoy_t = X_t / X_(t-12) - 1

Null if either month is missing; no month is filled.

Used by: core_month, core_yoy, cpi_blank_month, cpi_month, cpi_yoy, m2_month, m2_yoy, pce_month, pce_yoy

F-ffcomp Fed funds, compounded

growth = prod_d (1 + DFF_d / 36000)      (ACT/360, one factor per calendar day)
annual = growth ^ (365 / days) - 1

What a dollar earning the effective fed funds rate every day of the window would have returned, on the same footing as a staking yield.

Used by: ffcomp_365

F-spread-adj F-spread-naive Staking minus fed funds

spread_adj   = y_lst(window) - annual(F-ffcomp, same days)
spread_naive = y_lst(window) - mean(EFFR, same days)

The ledger prints both; verdicts use the like-for-like version.

Used by: spread_adj_365, spread_adj_365_dir, spread_adj_90, spread_adj_90_dir

Used by: spread_naive_365

F-rv Realized volatility

rv = stdev( ln(P_t / P_(t-1)) ) * sqrt(365)      (FX: sqrt(252))
sigma_d = rv / sqrt(365)

Used by: rv30_median, rv_365_btc, rv_365_eth, rv_365_eur, rv_365_near, rv_90_near, sigma_d

F-vrp Volatility risk premium (proxy)

vrp = DVOL_t - rv(forward 30 days)

Bitcoin and ether only, as context: no checked venue lists NEAR options to measure.

Used by: vrp_btc, vrp_eth

F-t3-gap Burn the fee-burn tripwire needs

burn_needed_t3   = t3_burn_pct / 100 * mint_per_day_365     (t3_burn_pct in rules.toml [params])
burn_multiple_t3 = burn_needed_t3 / burn_per_day_365

How much NEAR fees would have to burn each day for the confirming tripwire on fee burn to fire at today's issuance, and how many times the trailing year's daily burn that is. Both use the same trailing-year mint and burn as the burn share.

Used by: burn_multiple_t3, burn_needed_t3

F-mdd-365 Largest fall within the last year

mdd_365 = min_t ( P_t / max_(end-365d <= s <= t) P_s - 1 )      over closes in [end - 365 d, end)

Only closes within the trailing year count, so the high is one a holder could have bought at recently.

Used by: mdd_365

F-usd-12m One-year windows in dollars

ret12_w  = P(w_end) / P(w_end - 365 d) - 1      (stNEAR in dollars: NEAR price x stNEAR rate)
cash12_w = growth(F-ffcomp over the same days) - 1
_1y keys: windows with end - 365 d < w_end <= end, weekly

The share of weekly one-year windows in which stNEAR held within the band of its starting dollar value, or beat fed funds. The _1y keys count only windows that end within the trailing year.

Used by: n_windows_usd_1y, pct_beat_cash_1y, pct_within_2pp_1y

F-bis-rank The 10 most-traded currencies

rank = sort(currencies, by turnover_usd_bn_per_day, descending)[:10]      (BIS Triennial annex, net-net)

F-policy-latest What holding each currency pays now

The comparison economies' rates are in data/raw/bis/policy_rates_monthly.csv; China's and Hong Kong's come from the same BIS series in their own file, data/raw/bis/policy_rates_monthly_cn_hk.csv. For China, BIS's policy-rate series is the one-year Loan Prime Rate (its official one-year lending rate before the Loan Prime Rate replaced it); for Hong Kong it is the HKMA base rate, which follows the US rate under the peg. A currency whose area has no policy-rate series in data/raw/bis has no rate: its number is empty, and the reason names the files and the currency's exchange-rate regime (Singapore's central bank steers the exchange rate and sets no policy rate). Nothing is borrowed from another currency or carried forward.

The plain yearly rates the pay comparison uses, ranked: NEAR's liquid-staking yield over the past year against each currency's latest policy rate (the dollar's is fed funds now). A currency with no policy rate is not ranked. A description, not a claim: it has no verdict. The policy rate is a benchmark that cash rarely earns in full, and staking is paid in NEAR, so its dollar value moves with the price.

F-adv NEAR's advantage over the dollar, by month

E_M      = the 1st of M+1      (the supply sample that closes month M)
infl_M   = cpi_yoy_M - g_M      (CPIAUCSL year over year, F-yoy, minus NEAR's supply growth over the year to E_M, F-growth)
stake_M  = y_M - ff_M      (liquid staking, F-lst, minus fed funds compounded over the same trailing year, F-ffcomp)
A_M      = infl_M + stake_M = (cpi_yoy_M - g_M) + (y_M - ff_M)      (pp; no A when either part is missing)
side_M   = after if E_M > cut_date, else before
clean_M  = E_M - 365 d >= cut_date      (the month's whole trailing year is after the cut)
adv_share_le0 = 100 * count(A_M <= 0) / count(A_M)      (exactly zero counts as at or below zero)
adv_years     = floor((E_last - (E_first - 365 d)) / 365 d)

Rearranged it is (y - g) + (cpi - ff): a staker's gain in share of supply plus the dollar's real policy rate with its sign turned, so NEAR's dollar price is not in it. A month after the cut still holds mostly earlier issuance until its whole year is after it, so the clean count is printed beside the split and the rule reads every month. Consumer prices are the seasonally adjusted CPI-U, the series the money chart uses; it is a monthly average, centred about half a month before the supply year. Neighbouring months share most of their year, so the count of separate years is printed beside every month count.

F-cut-gap Since the issuance ceiling cut

M0         = the first month after cut_date's month whose CPI base CPI_(M0-1) is published, with a full-day supply sample on its 1st
M1         = the last month whose CPI_M1 is published, with a full-day supply sample on the 1st of M1+1
n          = months(M0..M1), inclusive
h2_near_g  = growth(supply on the 1st of M0, supply on the 1st of M1+1)      (annualized over block-time days, F-growth)
h2_cpi     = (CPI_M1 / CPI_(M0-1)) ^ (12 / n) - 1
h2_gap     = h2_cpi - h2_near_g      (pp; positive = NEAR grew more slowly)
alt        = the latest month before cut_date's month whose CPI level is published
h2_cpi_alt = (CPI_M1 / CPI_alt) ^ (12 / months(alt+1..M1)) - 1
h2_gap_alt = h2_cpi_alt - h2_near_g      (context; the rule never reads it)
gap_m      = ((CPI_m / CPI_(m-1)) ^ 12 - 1) - growth(supply on the 1st of m, supply on the 1st of m+1)      (each month; chart only)

The base month follows the shutdown's unpublished month, so the reading re-based on the last level published before the cut is printed beside it and never decides. NEAR's monthly growth is annualized over block-time days and CPI's by the twelfth power, a difference far below one month's noise.

F-vol-windows The one-year windows

e     = s + vol_horizon_days      (s a start day, e its end)
(a), (b): a daily close on every day s..e; DFF on every day in [s, e); LST samples dated s+1 and e+1
          y_w = lst_yield(LST at s+1, LST at e+1)      (the window's staking accrual, an outcome no decision reads)
C(k)  = prod_(j=0..k-1) (1 + DFF_(s+j) / 36000)      (a dollar from the close of s at fed funds, ACT/360)
u(k)  = (1 + y_w) ^ (k / 365.25)      (NEAR units growing at the window's staking yield)
p_k   = exp(L[o+k] - L[o])      (L the cumulative log price from vol_first_start, o = s - vol_first_start)
vol_years = floor((vol_last_end - vol_first_start) / 365 d)

A close dated d pairs with the supply sample dated the next day. The windows overlap, and the shuffles carry the same overlap.

F-vol-null Shuffled histories

blocks   = r_1..r_N cut into consecutive blocks of vol_null_block_days days      (the last may be shorter)
shuffle  = for i = (number of blocks - 1) down to 1: j = (rng.next() * (i + 1)) >> 32; swap blocks i and j
L*       = cumulative sum of the reordered returns      (vol_null_draws shuffles in order from one Prng(sim_seed) stream)
mean*    = the strategy's mean over windows on L*, with each window's real C and u
excess   = real mean - mean(mean*)
band     = type-7 quantiles of mean* at vol_rank_lo and vol_rank_hi
rank     = 100 * count(mean* < real mean) / vol_null_draws
band key = above if rank >= vol_rank_hi, below if rank <= vol_rank_lo, else inside
ladder   = the same shuffles of each venue's day records (F-perp-windows: close move, high and funding together),
           rerunning every window of the perp ladder (F-perp-ladder) on vol_perp_hl_* and vol_perp_bn_*
vol_perp_band = above if both venue bands are above, below if both are below, else inside

A shuffle keeps every daily move, the whole trend and each window's carry, and changes only the order of the blocks, so a rank can move only if the order of NEAR's moves mattered. Ranks, not standard deviations, because the shuffled results are lopsided.

F-vol-rally Selling into rallies

tau       = the first day in 1..H with p_tau >= 1 + vol_rally_pct / 100      (none: no sale)
t         = min(tau + 1, H)      (the sale is at the next close)
V_hold    = p_H * u(H)
V_a       = p_t * u(t) * C(H) / C(t) if tau exists, else V_hold
adv_a     = 100 * (V_a - V_hold)      (pp of the starting NEAR stake, against holding to the end)
vs_cash_a = 100 * (V_a - C(H))      (against selling at the start)

The sale is at the next close after the trigger, which needs no foresight. Even with no pattern in prices, selling on a rise before a deadline only moves gains between years: more modest wins, fewer large ones. The staking units at a sale use the whole window's yield, an outcome no decision reads.

F-vol-rebal Rebalancing to the desk's share

w      = sim_share / 100      (the desk's NEAR share)
on days k = vol_rebal_days, 2 * vol_rebal_days, ... < H:

R_reb  = the book at H
R_bh   = w * p_H * u(H) + (1 - w) * C(H)      (buy-and-hold)

theory = 100 * 0.5 * w * (1 - w) * sigma_w^2      (sigma_w: realized volatility of the window's own returns, pp of the book)

F-perp-windows The perp ladder's windows

v          = hl (Hyperliquid, hourly funding) or bn (Binance, eight-hourly funding)
fu[d]      = the sum of the funding rates settled for day d      (each stamp floored to its hour; a stamp at 00:00 UTC belongs to the day before, any other to its own day)
usable(d)  = every settlement of the day present, or on the hourly venue one missing, counted as zero      (vol_perp_<v>_partial_days counts those days)
e          = s + vol_horizon_days
s eligible = a perp bar on every day s..e; usable funding on every day s+1..e; DFF on every day in [s, e);
             LST samples dated s+1 and e+1 with lst_yield defined      (the start days of F-vol-windows, wherever the perp record reaches)
S0, S1     = the first eligible start and the last eligible end;  N = (S1 - S0) days
record t   = (c_t / c_(t-1), h_t / c_(t-1), fu_t),  t = 1..N      (c the perp's daily close, h = max(open, high))
p_k, hp_k  = c_(o+k) / c_o, h_(o+k) / c_o      (a window at offset o, k = 0..H)
LC[i]      = sum_(j < i) ln(1 + DFF_(S0+j) / 36000)      (a dollar sent on day k is worth exp(LC[o+H] - LC[o+k]) at the end; ACT/360, as F-ffcomp)
vol_perp_<v>_years = floor((vol_perp_<v>_last_end - vol_perp_<v>_first_start) / 365 d)

Both legs use the perpetual's own daily bars. The settlement stamped at midnight, the moment of the daily close, belongs to the day it closes, so a slice sold at a close is not credited it and a slice bought back at that close is; either way the difference is one settlement per trade, a third of a day's funding on Binance and a twenty-fourth on Hyperliquid. Consecutive windows overlap, sharing all but one day, so the count of separate years is printed beside every count of windows. The fed funds line stays on the calendar in every resampled history.

F-perp-ladder A ladder of short sales on a perpetual

units       the stake is one NEAR worth one dollar at the start close; the staked NEAR is never touched, so it cancels against holding
g = 1 + vol_perp_rung_pct / 100;  s = vol_perp_slice_pct / 100;  K = vol_perp_rungs;  maint = vol_perp_maint_pct / 100
start       B = 1;  j = 0;  Q = vol_perp_collateral * K * s      (the opening deposit, on the venue at the start close);  live
each day k = 1..H, with c = p_k, h = hp_k and the short z = j * s:
1 margin      if live and z > 0:  min_margin = min(min_margin, (Q - z h) / (maint z h))
              if Q - z h < maint z h: the venue closes the short at h;  liq_loss = max(Q - z h, 0);  Q = 0;  j = 0;  not live;  skip 2 and 3
2 funding     if live and z > 0:  Q += fu_t * z * (p_(k-1) + c) / 2      (the short held through the day, from yesterday's close)
3 trade       if live:  while j < K and c >= B g^(j+1): sell a slice at c (1 - vol_perp_slip_pct / 100), paying vol_perp_fee_pct / 100 of the proceeds;  j += 1
              else while j > 0 and c <= B g^(j-1): buy a slice back at c (1 + vol_perp_slip_pct / 100) plus the fee;  j -= 1
              then, if j = 0:  while c <= B / g:  B = B / g      (the base never moves up)
4 arrivals    a transfer due today joins Q if live; if not live it is sent home, arriving at min(k + vol_perp_transfer_days, H)
5 collateral  if live and k < H:  E = Q - z c;  E* = vol_perp_collateral * K s c
              if E + in flight < vol_perp_topup_at * E*: send E* - E - in flight, arriving at k + vol_perp_transfer_days
              else if nothing is in flight and E > vol_perp_sweep_at * E*: withdraw E - E*, home at min(k + vol_perp_transfer_days, H)
end         slices still short are bought back at the last close as in step 3
margin      min_margin = the lowest equity over the maintenance requirement at any day's high      (none when never short)

No foresight: every decision reads the day's close and the state, and the day's high is read only by the venue's margin check. Staked NEAR cannot be posted on a perpetual venue, so dollars worth the whole cap sit on the venue and follow the price even while the ladder is flat, because the next rise must find them there; dollars in transit earn nothing. The window starts at the first close with the opening deposit already on the venue: the holder sends it before the start, and its interest forgone is charged from the start close. Every later transfer takes the transfer time above. A margin ratio below one is a liquidation. Both venues are run with the same fee, slippage and maintenance margin.

F-perp-static A short that never trades

start close   sell vol_perp_static_pct / 100 of the stake short at 1 - vol_perp_slip_pct / 100, paying the fee
every day     z = vol_perp_static_pct / 100 while live; steps 1, 2, 4 and 5 of F-perp-ladder unchanged
              (the same opening deposit, collateral target vol_perp_collateral * K s c, top-ups, sweeps, margin check and interest)
end close     buy it back as in step 3
swing         = adv - adv_static      (each window, pp of the starting NEAR stake)
vol_perp_<v>_swing = the mean swing over the venue's windows

Both positions collect funding and pay for the same dollars on the venue, and the short that never trades carries the ladder's average exposure. What is left in the swing is what selling after rises and buying back after falls earned or lost, including the extra funding the ladder collects by being short more when NEAR is higher, net of its extra fees and slippage. It gains when NEAR swings and comes back, and loses when NEAR runs one way: up past the cap, or down while the ladder sits flat. Its size is half the ladder's most, fixed before a window starts.

F-perp-kept Funding and what it left

venue    = Q + in flight + withdrawn - deposited      (face values: the venue's profit and loss)
interest = each deposit compounded at fed funds from its send day to the end, less each withdrawal compounded from its arrival, less the face difference
adv      = venue - interest      (the strategy minus holding the same staked NEAR and the same dollars at fed funds)
funding  = the sum of step 2 of F-perp-ladder
costs    = fees plus slippage on every trade
kept     = funding - costs - interest - liq_loss      (the funding left after the position's own costs)
price    = adv - kept

Context, not a test: a short that never trades collects most of the same funding, so its kept is printed beside the ladder's and neither decides anything. Means are over the venue's windows in points of the starting NEAR stake; costs, interest and liquidation losses are printed as positive amounts.

F-perp-redraw Redrawn histories, centred

blocks      = the day records t = 1..N cut into consecutive blocks of vol_null_block_days days      (a record keeps its close move, its high and its funding)
history d   = append block b = (rng.next() * nblocks) >> 32 until at least N days are filled, then cut to N
              (vol_null_draws histories from one Prng(sim_seed) stream; blocks can repeat)
m_d         = the mean swing over every window, the ladder and the short that never trades both rerun on history d
m_bar       = mean_d m_d      (vol_perp_<v>_swing_raw_mean)
centred_d   = m_d - m_bar + vol_perp_<v>_swing
swing_lo, swing_hi = type-7 quantiles of centred_d at vol_rank_lo and vol_rank_hi
swing_share = 100 * count(centred_d > 0) / vol_null_draws
swing_band  = above if swing_share >= vol_rank_hi, below if swing_share <= vol_rank_lo, else inside
vol_perp_swing_band = above if both venues are above, below if both are below, else inside

A shuffle keeps every day, so it cannot change a level much; a redraw can leave out the richest months or repeat the poorest, which asks whether the result would hold with other months. Drawing months with repeats also breaks NEAR's swings longer than a block and changes each path's drift, which moves the redrawn average by itself, so the redraws are centred on the real result and read only for their spread.

F-perp-coinbase A US-regulated NEAR perpetual

record = Coinbase Derivatives' NEAR Perp, NER-20DEC30-CDE: its daily candles and one snapshot of its product record
vol_perp_cb_listed       = the record's new_at, as a UTC day
vol_perp_cb_days         = daily bars from vol_perp_cb_listed to the last full UTC day
vol_perp_cb_contract     = contract_size (NEAR per contract)
vol_perp_cb_oi_usd       = open_interest (contracts) * contract_size * index_price, at the snapshot
vol_perp_cb_funding_interval = funding_interval, in hours
vol_perp_cb_short_margin_overnight, vol_perp_cb_short_margin_intraday = 100 * the record's short margin rates, overnight and intraday
vol_perp_cb_margin_rise  = 100 * (1 - m) / (1 + m),  m = the overnight short margin rate
                           (a short backed by dollars equal to its value at the sale, with no top-up, has equity 1 - r
                            after a rise r and must hold m (1 + r): the two meet at this r)
vol_perp_cb_access_read  = the day Coinbase's US eligibility pages were read: the retrieval date of the declared constant
                           cb_us_derivatives_access
no rule reads these keys

Hyperliquid and Binance, the two venues the ladder is tested on, are reported to exclude US persons. Coinbase Derivatives is a US-regulated futures exchange, and US customers trade it through Coinbase Financial Markets, in dollars: its NEAR contract, listed 2026-02-28, holds 500 NEAR, sets a funding rate every 1 h and had about $7.54 million of open positions at the snapshot, so an approved US holder can run the ladder there. Coinbase's help pages, read 2026-11-13, say access needs an approved application (Coinbase checks age, experience, employment, income and net worth) and an eligible address, set each customer's position limits by income and net worth, and may not be available in every jurisdiction; they name no US state as excluded (the quotes). Its record holds 259 days of daily bars, short of the one-year window the test needs, and Coinbase publishes its funding history only on request, so neither claim reads it.

The ladder's collateral rule covers Coinbase's margin: it keeps dollars worth 1.00× the most it can be short on the venue, against a short margin of 56.2% of the short's value overnight and 20.0% intraday. That overnight margin is far above the test's 5% maintenance level, and the record read gives no separate maintenance rate for Coinbase, so with no top-up a short backed by dollars equal to its value meets the overnight margin after a rise of about 28%. Coinbase's funding formula follows the contract's premium over the spot price and has no fixed interest term, so by its formula a short there is not paid a set rate while the two trade close together, whatever sign the rate has in a given hour.

F-sim-pool The days a simulated year is drawn from

a_d = P(d) / P(d - 1)                 every calendar day d in the window (NEAR's daily close)
b_d = X(d) / X(previous fixing)       on DEXUSEU fixing days, else 1
a~_d = a_d / mean(a),  b~_d = b_d / mean(b)      (demeaned in gross terms, never in logs)

Dividing by the average gross move removes the window's own trend and keeps its swings, skew, tails and same-day co-movement. NEAR's close is at midnight UTC and the euro's fixing at noon in New York, so a same-day pair is measured hours apart.

F-sim-path One simulated year

path i: sim_horizon_days draws of one joint day index j        (xoshiro128** seeded by splitmix32)
G_i = prod a~_j,  X_i = prod b~_j,  h_i = 1 if the running product of a~ is ever <= sim_half
G_i = G_i / mean(G),  X_i = X_i / mean(X)                        (moment matched: the average year ends at 1)

Days are drawn with replacement and each draw keeps NEAR's move and the euro's move from the same day. The same draws serve every setting of the controls, so moving one slides the outcomes instead of reshuffling them.

D_i = w V u_i                                    (F-sim-benefit)
w share in NEAR, s dollar share of the cash, k = 1 staked (0 not), mu assumed price change, c costs

The NEAR part is bought with dollars and euros in the cash's own proportions, so the only choice is NEAR or cash. Staking rewards are paid in NEAR, so their dollar value moves with the price. This is the held unit; F-sim-rebal gives the reset one.

     + price  w V mu (1 + k y)
     - costs  w V c

The average is computed in closed form, never as an average of simulated years: simulation noise on the average is larger than the carry itself. The bracket cells swap one input at a time (the price assumption, interest parity for the euro, an all-dollar desk, the one-year Treasury).

F-sim-drift The price assumptions on offer

price flat on average     mu = 0                                   (the default)
demand flat in dollars    mu_v = 1 / (1 + g) - 1                   g = g_365 / 100

The price change is an assumption the reader chooses; it is never measured from past prices. Price flat treats NEAR as the model treats the euro (the price expected unchanged, each holding earning its own carry) and assumes the price already reflects published issuance. Demand flat in dollars is the quantity-theory view with no growth in demand. The evidence favours neither, and they give the expected benefit opposite signs, so the page shows both, with the thesis's implication, whichever is selected.

S = sort(u);  q(p) = S[h] + (h - floor h)(S[h+1] - S[h]),  h = (N - 1) p      (type 7)
median q(0.5);  bad year q(0.05);  good year q(0.95);  p_beat = share of u > 0

u is the held unit (F-sim-unit) or the reset one (F-sim-rebal), whichever the desk runs. Held without trading, every dollar figure is the per-dollar result times the NEAR part, so holding more NEAR changes the size of the outcome, not the odds. Reset every 30 days, the share also sets how much each reset trades, so the odds move a little with the share (c31). A shortfall can exceed the NEAR part itself, because it is measured against the interest the cash would otherwise have earned.

F-sim-be Break-evens, exact

mean break-even    mu_E* = (1 + R_B + c) / (1 + k y) - 1
per year           mu_i  = (1 + R_B,i + c) / ((1 + k y) G_i) - 1;   median break-even = median(mu_i)
break-even cost    c*    = (1 + mu)(1 + k y) - 1 - R_B
reset mode (F-sim-rebal), with h = rt / (2 bp), c = (rt + cu) / bp and Tbar = mean(T_i) held at the state's value:
break-even cost    r*    = (E_reb - w cu / bp) / (w + Tbar / 2)        (the round-trip cost that erases the expected benefit, custody as entered)
mean break-even    mu where (M0(mu) - K0) - w c - h Tbar = 0           (bisection)
median break-even  the N/2-th smallest per-year break-even              (bisection over the years still undecided)

Both reset-mode bisections stay inside the price assumption's range on the control. The median break-even is exact while each year's result rises with the price, which a trading cost can bend only by less than the cost.

F-sim-rebal Strategy (b) in the desk: resetting the NEAR share

R = vol_rebal_days, H = sim_horizon_days;  periods l_p = R, R, ..., and H minus the resets' days      (a reset at R, 2R, ... below H)
pw(r, n)  = r to the integer power n, by squaring;  dayf(a, H) = the day root of a by bisection: pw(dayf(a, H), H) ~ a
            (no pow, exp or log, so the browser and Python agree bit for bit)
kG = dayf(1 / mean(G_raw), H),  kX = dayf(1 / mean(X_raw), H)      (F-sim-path's moment matching, spread over the days)
period p of path i:  A_p = pw(dayf(near_f, H), l_p) pw(kG, l_p) g_p,i      near_f = (1 + mu)(1 + k y)
                     U_p = pw(dayf(1 + R_U, H), l_p)
                     E_p = pw(dayf(1 + r_E, H), l_p) pw(kX, l_p) x_p,i      (g_p,i, x_p,i: the path's own products of a~ and b~ over p)
start:  N = w,  C_U = (1 - w) s,  C_E = (1 - w)(1 - s),  B_U = s,  B_E = 1 - s,  T = 0
each p: N = N A_p;  C_U = C_U U_p;  C_E = C_E E_p;  B_U = B_U U_p;  B_E = B_E E_p
        reset (not after the last period): M = N + C_U + C_E;  d = N - w M;  N = w M;  C_U = C_U + s d;  C_E = C_E + (1 - s) d;  T = T + |d|
u_i = ((N + C_U + C_E) - (B_U + B_E) - h T) / w - c,   h = rt / (2 bp)      (each reset trade pays half a round trip)
E_reb, E_bh = the same recursion with g = x = 1, with and without resets
edge     = V (E_reb - E_bh)                                  sim_reb_edge_usd
turnover = V Tbar,  Tbar = mean(T_i)                         sim_reb_turnover_usd
mean     = F-sim-mean + edge - V h Tbar;   costs = F-sim-mean's costs - V h Tbar

The NEAR part is reset to its share at the same marks the real-history test of H10 uses: a surplus of NEAR is sold into dollars and euros in the cash's own proportions, and a shortfall is bought from them. The mean is exact: each period's draws are independent of the past and average one, and every holding is linear in the last period's, so the recursion run once at the average draw gives it. Only the turnover, the one term with an absolute value, is simulated. Trading costs are charged against the year's end value, not netted out of the holdings as each reset trades. With days drawn independently, a fall is as likely to continue as to reverse, so the resets add nothing in expectation and the edge is the carry they trim. This is the strategy H10 tests on NEAR's real history (F-vol-rebal).

Why the desk resets: three ways of selling NEAR's swings were run on the one-year windows they all share: selling after a 25% rise and waiting in dollars (selling into rallies), resetting the NEAR part to its share every 30 days, and the perp ladder (shorting slices of the stake on a perpetual future as NEAR rises and buying them back as it falls). Resetting came out ahead of the other two on both venues' spans. In percentage points (pp) of the staked NEAR's value against simply holding it, over Binance's 1,317 shared windows it ended +0.21 pp, against −16.23 pp for the perp ladder and −42.20 pp for selling into rallies; over Hyperliquid's 741, +21.71 pp against +16.88 pp and +10.94 pp. None of the three beat chance against NEAR's shuffled histories, so the order says which suited NEAR's past, not which captures its swings. (F-vol-compare)

Desk simulation: method

The film's last scene, as a model. Its formulas are the F-sim anchors above; every figure here is the default state, and every one is in the registry below.

A trading desk holds $500 million it will not deploy for 365 days: 76% in dollar cash and 24% in euro cash. That split is a benchmark proxy from the two currencies' shares of foreign-exchange trading, not any desk's holdings. The mix moves 3.7% ($18.50 million) into liquid-staked NEAR, bought with dollars and euros in the same proportions, and the baseline keeps everything in cash. The baseline is held as it is and the mix resets its NEAR part, as the paragraph below says; both are in nominal dollars, and deflating both by the same price index would leave their difference the same in real terms.

Dollar cash earns the effective fed funds rate, 3.88% (4.01% over a year, compounded). Euro cash earns €STR, 2.44% (2.51%). The NEAR part earns NEAR's liquid-staking yield over the last year, 4.13%, paid in NEAR. Every rate is held where it is today. The one-year Treasury, 4.38% (4.43% as an annual rate), replaces fed funds only in one bracket cell and one sensitivity row.

Each of the 20,000 simulated years is 365 days drawn at random, with replacement, from the last 365 days to 2026-11-09, each draw keeping NEAR's move and the euro's move from the same day; the alternative window is the last 90 days. Each day's move is divided by the window's average move, so the window's trend is gone and its swings remain, and each year is then scaled so the average year ends where the price assumption says. As a check, the simulated years spread NEAR's price by 103.5% (the standard deviation of its log), against a measured volatility of 103.3% over the last year.

The expected benefit is exact, from the closed form; the typical year, the tails and the dots come from the simulated years. The price change is the reader's assumption, and the default is flat on average. One year of data pins an average price change only to within about 103.3% either way, so no past return is offered as a forecast. The other assumptions on offer: demand flat in dollars (−2.42%) and the thesis's implication (3.15% from money, 1.20% from prices), which assumes demand for NEAR keeps pace with dollar money, something nothing on this site measures.

Every 30 days the mix resets its NEAR part to 3.7% of the desk: after a rise it sells NEAR into dollars and euros, after a fall it buys, the strategy H10 tests on NEAR's real history (F-sim-rebal). Over the year the resets trade $51.2 million at each day's closing price, paying only the trading cost entered on the controls. In these simulated years each day is drawn at random, so a fall is as likely to continue as to reverse, and the resets change the expected benefit only by −$180: they win the choppy years and lose the trending ones, so the typical year narrows and the bad years deepen. Whether NEAR's real swings reverse often enough to pay is the question of H10: over all 1,328 of NEAR's real one-year windows, not only those the three strategies share (F-vol-compare), the same resets came out +0.90 pp of the NEAR stake against holding on average, inside the range shuffled histories produce. A control on the desk holds the NEAR part without trading instead; the table after the risk figures sets the two side by side.

What this leaves out

  • An exchange or custodian failing.
  • The liquid-staking contract failing, or its token trading below what it redeems for.
  • Rates changing during the year: every rate is held where it is today.
  • Trading and custody costs, unless entered above.
  • Accounting and capital treatment: ask your auditor and your regulator.
  • A crypto desk needs cash most when crypto is falling, which is when NEAR is likely down and thin.
  • The price impact of the resets: they trade $51.2 million over the year at each day's closing price, paying only the trading cost entered above.

The desk's charts

  • c30 100 simulated years for the $18.50 million NEAR part: ahead in 47, behind in 53
  • c31 Resetting a larger NEAR share scales the outcome far more than the odds
  • c32 Getting out: about 3.1 days to sell the $18.50 million NEAR part at a whole median day of Coinbase volume
  • c33 What moves the answer: rates and staking move the expected value; the window and the resets move the spread

This is a scenario tool, not investment advice. It shows what the measured yield, volatility and liquidity imply under an assumption you choose; it does not predict NEAR's price.

Verdict rules

Rules live in thesis/rules.toml. Each claim is checked in this order: a null input gives Not computed, then Not testable, Supported, Refuted; anything else is Partly.

H1 NEAR's supply grows slower than major currencies' money

NEAR is deflationary compared to other currencies.

Supportedrule and result
Not computed if
n_fiat_money < 7
Supported if
gap_m2 > 0 and h1_gap_med > 0
Refuted if
gap_m2 ≤ 0
Partly
otherwise
Result
gap_m2 +3.23 pp h1_gap_med +2.31 pp h1_n_faster 9 n_fiat_money 10 m2_yoy 5.71% g_365 2.48%
Decided by
gap_m2 > 0 and h1_gap_med > 0
Margin
3.23 pp from the deciding threshold, on how much slower NEAR supply grew than US money, each over its latest year
Test
Over the latest year of each (NEAR's supply to the latest chain sample, each currency's money to its latest month), did NEAR's supply grow slower than US broad money and than the median broad-money growth of the most-traded currencies?
Metrics
gap_m2, h1_gap_med, h1_n_faster, n_fiat_money, m2_yoy, g_365
Charts
c21 c11

H2 Since the issuance ceiling cut, NEAR's supply has grown slower than US prices

NEAR is deflationary relative to the dollar

Supportedrule and result
Supported if
h2_gap > 0
Refuted if
h2_gap < 0
Partly
otherwise
Result
h2_gap +1.69 pp h2_near_g 2.48% h2_cpi 4.17% h2_from 2025-12-01 h2_to 2026-11-01 h2_months_slower 8 h2_months_read 11 cut_date 2025-10-29
Decided by
h2_gap > 0
Margin
1.69 pp from the deciding threshold, on how much slower NEAR supply grew than US prices after the ceiling cut, from the first month with a CPI base, a year
Test
From the first month after the issuance ceiling cut that US CPI-U can match to the latest CPI month, did NEAR's supply grow slower than US consumer prices, both annualized over the same months?

h2_gap, h2_near_g, h2_cpi, h2_from, h2_to, h2_months_slower, h2_months_read, cut_date

H3 Staking pays about 0.25 pp more than fed funds

Current staking rewards of 4.13% are approximately 0.25% higher than the effective federal funds rate of 3.88%.

Supportedrule and result
Supported if
spread_adj_365 > 0 and spread_adj_365 ≤ 1.0
Refuted if
spread_adj_365 ≤ 0
Partly
if spread_adj_365 > 1.0
Result

Decided by
spread_adj_365 > 0 and spread_adj_365 ≤ 1.0
Margin
0.32 pp from the deciding threshold, on staking minus fed funds, like for like, last year
Test
Over the last 365 days, did liquid-staking yield beat compounded fed funds by more than zero and at most 1 pp (like for like)?
Metrics
spread_adj_365, y_lst_365, ffcomp_365, spread_naive_365, effr_mean_365

H4 NEAR's supply-and-staking edge over the dollar holds as rates move

Though both the inflation rate and fed rate change, they stay in balance over time.

Supportedrule and result
Not computed if
adv_months_before < 1 or adv_months_after < 1
Supported if
adv_share_le0 ≤ 40
Refuted if
adv_share_le0 > 40
Partly
otherwise
Result
adv_share_le0 0.00% adv_months_le0 0 adv_months 42 adv_months_before 31 adv_months_after 11 adv_mean_before +2.10 pp adv_mean_after +1.70 pp adv_years 4 adv_months_clean_after 0
Decided by
adv_share_le0 ≤ 40
Margin
40.0 pp from the deciding threshold, on share of months NEAR's advantage over the dollar was at or below zero
Test
NEAR's edge over the dollar is US CPI-U inflation minus NEAR's supply growth, plus liquid-staking yield minus compounded fed funds, each over the same trailing year, read every month, in years ending before and after the issuance ceiling cut; NEAR's dollar price is not part of it. Was it at or below zero in no more than 40% of the months?
Metrics
adv_share_le0, adv_months_le0, adv_months, adv_months_before, adv_months_after, adv_mean_before, adv_mean_after, adv_years, adv_months_clean_after

Test
No options venue I could check lists NEAR, so the test sells NEAR's swings on a perpetual: keep the NEAR staked, sell 10% of the stake short at the daily close after each 10% rise, at most 5 times, and buy each slice back after a 10% fall. Over every one-year window with full data, did this ladder end ahead of a short of 25% of the stake held all year with the same dollars on the venue, after funding, fees, slippage, interest and any liquidation? Supported if its average lead stays above zero in at least 97.5% of 1,000 histories redrawn from blocks of 30 of NEAR's own days and centred on the real result, on both Hyperliquid and Binance; refuted if in 2.5% or fewer on both.

Known gaps and unverified items

  • Slashing unverified · affects H6, c14

    As far as I can tell NEAR does not slash validator stake today, but I have not confirmed it in the protocol spec or the nearcore source. If slashing exists, liquid staking carries a loss path that none of the yield figures include.

    Would resolve it: Cite the nearcore code path or the Nomicon section that governs slashing, pinned to a commit.

    Nomicon, the NEAR protocol specification

  • LiNEAR instant-exit depth not measured · affects H6, c14

    Meta Pool's instant-unstake pool holds 75,887 NEAR, read from its contract. LiNEAR's equivalent was not measured, so the same-day liquidity row of the sweep checklist is marked partial.

    Would resolve it: Read LiNEAR's instant-unstake liquidity and fee from its contract at the same height as the Meta Pool read.

  • Binance and Bybit options, not checkable from the US not checkable · affects H8, c15

    Binance's options API and Bybit's public endpoints refuse requests from US addresses, so the venue table marks them not checked rather than no. Unchecked venues: 2.

    Would resolve it: A venue check from a non-US network, with each venue's HTTP status.

  • A NEAR perpetual for US holders, too new to test open · affects H8, H10, c26

    The ladder is tested on Hyperliquid and Binance, which are reported to exclude US persons (neither's terms were read first-hand here), and Kraken's own instrument record lists only non-US platforms for its NEAR perpetual. Coinbase Derivatives has listed a US-regulated NEAR perpetual-style future since 2026-02-28, which US customers trade in dollars through Coinbase Financial Markets, so an approved US holder can run the ladder there. Coinbase's help pages, read 2026-11-13, say access needs an approved application and an eligible address, set position limits by income and net worth, and may not be available in every jurisdiction; they name no US state as excluded. Its record holds 259 days of daily bars, short of the one-year window the test needs, and Coinbase publishes its funding history only on request, so neither claim reads it.

    Would resolve it: A year of Coinbase's NEAR perpetual record with its hourly funding, run through the same test as Hyperliquid and Binance.

    Coinbase: US perpetual-style futures · Coinbase: US derivatives eligibility

  • near.com's perpetual market and fees unverified · affects H8, c26

    near.com's own perpetual market list and fees could not be read; the test uses Hyperliquid's public book, which near.com says it routes to.

    Would resolve it: near.com's NEAR perpetual market and fee schedule, read first-hand.

  • Kraken's funding rate period unverified · affects c26

    Kraken's published funding rate is used only for its sign, because the period it is quoted for was not confirmed first-hand.

    Would resolve it: Kraken's documentation or a first-hand read that states the period its NEAR funding rate is quoted for.

  • Purpose of the treasury outflow unverified

    The treasury.near balance, column treasury_near in data/raw/rpc/history_samples.csv, dropped sharply in one quarter this year. I could not find a published purpose. Supply growth is unaffected; sell pressure might not be.

    Would resolve it: A treasury report or an on-chain trace that names where the NEAR went.

  • Origin of the quoted staking rate unverified · affects H3, c01

    The hypothesis quotes a staking rate without saying where it came from. The ledger tests the claim against the measured trailing-year liquid staking yield, 4.13%, and shows both.

    Would resolve it: Name the dashboard and the date the quoted rate came from.

  • BigQuery freshness depends on BigQuery · affects c05, c16

    Exact burn figures need the public NEAR BigQuery dataset, whose latest block date is 2026-11-10; where it has no data the figure is labelled sampled or upper bound.

    Would resolve it: The BigQuery dataset keeping pace with the chain (the data page shows its lag in days).

    NEAR docs: BigQuery public dataset

  • Permission to publish Intents Explorer aggregates open · affects c06

    The NEAR Intents Explorer comparison needs partner access and written permission to publish under its terms. It is not included, so the Intents volume chart rests on DefiLlama alone.

    Would resolve it: Partner access and a written answer from NEAR Intents.

    NEAR Intents Explorer API documentation

  • Bank of England money series open · affects c21

    Sterling money here is the wide aggregate the Bank publishes as M4; the narrower version that excludes intermediate financial companies is the closer match for other currencies' broad money, but its series code is not confirmed.

    Would resolve it: The confirmed Bank of England series code for the narrower aggregate.

Terms notes by source

NEAR mainnet JSON-RPC
Public JSON-RPC; chain data is public. FastNEAR rate-limits archival calls (HTTP 429), so samples are cached append-only.
FRED, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis
Keyless FRED graph CSV. FRED terms of use apply; each series is credited to its original publisher (BLS, BEA, Federal Reserve Board, New York Fed). FRED keeps no vintages here, and BLS published no October 2025 CPI.
BIS data portal (policy rates, including China and Hong Kong; consumer prices)
Keyless BIS SDMX API; BIS statistics may be reused with the source credited. Argentina has no policy rate after 2025-07-10; Australia's CPI is quarterly.
Binance spot klines (NEARUSDT, BTCUSDT, ETHUSDT)
Binance public market-data host; Binance terms of use apply. Quotes are in USDT, not USD (cross-checked against Coinbase NEAR-USD).
Coinbase Exchange candles (NEAR-USD)
Coinbase Exchange public market data; Coinbase terms apply. Series starts 2022-09-01.
Options venue check (Deribit, OKX, Aevo, Bybit, Binance)
Public exchange APIs. Bybit and Binance block US addresses; an unreachable venue is recorded as not checked, never as no.
Deribit DVOL (BTC, ETH implied volatility)
Deribit public API; context only (no NEAR implied volatility exists).
Hyperliquid NEAR perpetual (hourly funding, daily and hourly candles)
Hyperliquid public info endpoint (read-only, no account or key); Hyperliquid terms apply. Funding starts at the listing, 2023-11-01; daily candles before it carry no trades and are left out; the venue serves only its latest 5,000 candles, so the hourly file accumulates across pulls. Used for claim H8 and the perp ladder. Hyperliquid's terms are reported to count US persons among Restricted Persons (secondary text, not read first-hand); reading its public data needs no account.
Kraken Derivatives PF_NEARUSD perpetual (hourly funding, daily candles)
Kraken Derivatives public market data; Kraken terms apply. Funding history is served for a rolling year only, so the funding file accumulates from the first pull; candles start at the listing, 2022-06-13. Read only for the sign of funding over the latest year the three venues share; its rate's period is not confirmed, so no rate is printed.
Binance USD-M NEARUSDT perpetual (8-hour funding, daily candles)
Binance public bulk-data host; Binance terms apply. Every file is checked against the sha256 Binance publishes for it. Funding is published in monthly files only, so it ends with the last published month; quotes are in USDT. The longer record for the perp ladder; Binance futures are reported not to be open to US persons.
NEAR perpetual contract terms (Hyperliquid, Kraken Derivatives)
Public exchange APIs. A snapshot of each venue's NEAR contract (leverage, margin tiers, funding parameters) and live context (funding, open interest, mark) at fetch time, not a history.
Coinbase Derivatives NEAR Perp, NER-20DEC30-CDE (daily candles, contract snapshot)
Coinbase public market data (no account or key); Coinbase terms apply. Coinbase Derivatives, LLC is a CFTC-regulated exchange, reached by US customers through the futures commission merchant Coinbase Financial Markets; this is a separate source from the Coinbase Exchange spot candles. One contract is 500 NEAR, margined in US dollars. Daily candles start at the listing, 2026-02-28, with volume in contracts. Coinbase publishes no keyless funding history (the exchange's funding-rate endpoint needs an API key; Coinbase supplies the history on request), so funding appears only as the current rate in the snapshot. US customers Coinbase approves can trade this NEAR perpetual, so an approved US holder can run the perp ladder here; Coinbase's help pages (Wayback captures of 2026-11-13) say access needs an approved application and an eligible address and may not be available in all jurisdictions, and name no US state as excluded. Its record is shorter than one year, so no one-year window exists yet and no claim reads it.
DefiLlama (NEAR Intents volume and fees)
DefiLlama open API. The volume adapter reads a Dune table maintained by NEAR, so it is not independent of Dune; the 3 most recent days are provisional.
NEAR Intents Explorer API (1Click daily aggregates)
1ClickSwap API Terms 4.1(e): API data may not be stored for more than 24 hours, so rows never leave memory and only daily aggregates are written. Publishing them waits for written permission from NEAR Intents.
Fiat money panel: central banks and their statistics portals (FRED, ECB, BoJ, BoE, OECD, SNB, RBA, BoC, HKMA, SingStat)
Keyless public statistics; each series is credited to its publisher on the data page. The BoE and HKMA responses are archived unchanged under each currency's _raw folder; every other series records the full request URL and the SHA-256 of the response.
BIS Triennial Central Bank Survey 2025 (FX turnover by currency)
Keyless BIS SDMX API; BIS statistics may be reused with the source credited. Picks the ten most-traded currencies for the money panel.
BigQuery public dataset crypto_near_mainnet_us
Google Cloud public dataset published by NEAR; query outputs only are committed. tokens_burnt overstates the supply burn by the developer gas rebate (burnt_gas_reward) only before HSP-027 took effect (the burnt_gas_reward change in rpc/protocol_changes.csv); from that block gross equals net.
Declared constants (nearcore, core-contracts, eCFR, press, Coinbase help)
Quoted under fair use with links to pinned source revisions.

Supply reconciliation

A diagnostic: BigQuery's total supply against the RPC's at the same heights. It decides no verdict.
